one_month_reasoning: These events fall inside the window to Oct 30: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, which comes after the Sep 17 hike with the 10-year at 5.24% (supervisor, FRED); Q3 reports from peers VRT, GEV and Schneider; and hyperscaler Q3 capex commentary in the last week of October. Eaton's own Q3 report is listed for Nov 3 before the open. The supervisor calls that date unconfirmed and gives it 25-30% odds of landing by Oct 30, since Eaton reported on Oct 31 in 2023 and 2024. My search snippet from MarketBeat labels Nov 3 as confirmed, so the evidence conflicts, and I put the in-window odds at ~15-20%. Management said at Laguna that Q3 is tracking to the high end of guidance, so an in-window print would lean slightly positive, but mostly it adds variance. The rate and capex events cut both ways, and the stock has already recovered from ~$395 to $432, so I apply no momentum or reversal tilt. The distribution is a lognormal with median ~$433 and sigma 11.5% for the month (39%/3.5 = 11.1%, nudged up for the cluster of events). It is essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%) and EV/sales (40%). P/E: pro-forma ex-Mobility NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of ~$16.86 x 25.5x = $430. EV/sales: ex-Mobility NTM sales ~$36.3B x 5.0x = EV $181.5B, less ~$17.3B net debt, over ~381M post-split-off shares = $431. Blended fair value ~$430, about spot (was $446 in round 1).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Sep 2027 ~$16.86 (0.25 x 2027 pro-forma ex-Mobility $15.25 + 0.75 x 2028E $17.40) x 25.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Mobility H1 2026 segment operating profit was $198M, so ~$400M/yr, or ~$330M after tax, which is ~$0.85/share on 389.5M shares. The offsets are ~8.5M retired shares (worth ~+2%, ~$0.3) and ~$40M of interest saved on $1.1B of debt paydown (~$0.1). The net is ~$0.45-0.5, which matches the supervisor's figure.

Pro-forma 2027 x ~1.14. That is below the 2026-to-2027 step, because MS expects hyperscaler capex growth to slow to +14% in 2028. It is supported by capacity already being added (Bellevue plant, 200+ hires; NC +300 jobs) and by MV switchgear lead times still 2-4x pre-pandemic norms. Those point to volume limited by capacity rather than demand through 2028.

Today ~27.4x 2027E. I take off ~1.9 turns. The AI-power group de-rated after the Sep 14 episode, and growth decelerates into 2028. On top of that, the 10-year is at 5.24% and the Fed hiked on Sep 17 (supervisor-verified). That goes half a turn below the supervisor's 26x, and I stay above industrial averages because of the multi-year backlog.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: Ex-Mobility NTM sales Sep 2027 ~$36.3B x 5.0x = EV $181.5B; net debt ~$17.3B; ~381M shares after split-off

inputs_detail.derivation: $36.63B less ~$3.3B of Mobility, assuming consensus carries a full year of it

Current EV is ~$188B ($432.28 x 389.5M + $19.9B net debt). Less the ~$5.1B deal value of Mobility, that leaves ~$183B, which is ~5.5x ex-Mobility 2027 sales. I compress this ~9% for decelerating growth and a 5%+ 10-year.

$19.9B at Jun 30 (debt $20.61B less $0.70B cash). Deduct $1.1B of RMT cash to debt and ~$4.3B of FCF. Add back ~$1.65B of dividends and ~$0.95B for COL Group (EUR 810M). No buybacks: the 10-Q says none in 2026.
389.5M less ~8.5M tendered. The Mobility deal value is ~$5.1B; less $1.1B of cash, ~$4.0B of SpinCo equity goes to ETN holders, exchanged at a typical ~7-10% discount at ~$432.

bear.story: Hyperscalers signal 2027-28 capex digestion and data center orders roll over against huge comps. 2028 EPS is cut toward $15.5-16. With the 10-year above 5%, the multiple de-rates to ~19-20x NTM (GLJ's 'cyclical priced as secular' critique). The margin step-up needed in H2 2026 is missed.

base.story: 2026 guidance is met, and pro-forma 2027 EPS is ~$15.25 after the Mobility split-off closes in Q1 2027 (~8.5M shares retired, $1.1B to debt). Backlog converts as Bellevue and the European capacity (COL) ramp. The multiple settles near 25.5-26x NTM EPS of ~$16.9 while rates stay high.

bull.story: 2027 hyperscaler capex rises significantly, and Boyd liquid-cooling and 800V DC/SST orders land. Price/cost turns into a tailwind in 2027. EPS revisions run toward $16+ pro forma for 2027 and $19+ for 2028, and the stock re-rates to ~30x as a grid-to-chip platform, helped if rates ease.

thesis_break_reason: About 24% below today, below the September low (~$390-395) and near the $312 52-week low. $330 is ~19.6x pro-forma ex-Mobility NTM EPS of ~$16.9. At that multiple only estimate cuts explain the price: data center order cancellations, negative Electrical Americas rolling orders, or a failed H2 margin step-up. With the 10-year above 5%, a multiple de-rating alone could reach the mid-$300s, so I would treat a trade at $330 as a thesis break only if order or backlog data confirms it. Alt-data tells: hiring freezes at the new switchgear plants, or falling MV switchgear lead times.

reasoning: Round 2 changes come mainly from the supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified against the filings. (1) The Mobility/Dana deal is a split-off by exchange offer (10-Q, Form 425), so there is no price drop. It retires ~8.5M shares, based on the ~$5.1B deal value less the $1.1B cash, and costs ~3% of EPS. Mobility is ~$3.3B of annual sales and ~$400M of segment profit (Q2 release). I agree with the supervisor's ~$0.5 net dilution, so the 2027 pro-forma base falls from $15.75 to $15.25 and NTM EPS at the horizon from $17.4 to ~$16.9. (2) There are no buybacks in 2026 and the RMT cash goes to debt, so my net-debt bridge is rebuilt at ~$17.3B. (3) The 10-year is at 5.24% after the Sep 17 Fed hike, so I cut my P/E to 25.5x, half a turn below the supervisor's 26x, because the rate backdrop hits the highest-multiple names first. (4) I rebuilt EV/sales on ex-Mobility sales and post-split-off shares rather than dropping it. Both methods now land at ~$430, down from $446. On the lane question, my alt-data points to volume rather than just direction. Eaton is adding capacity (Bellevue 370k sq ft, 200+ hires; NC +300 jobs), and MV switchgear lead times remain 2-4x pre-pandemic norms, with trade trackers saying many channels are booked past 2028. That says 2027 growth is limited by capacity, not demand, which supports the ~12-14% 2028 growth I assume even as hyperscaler capex growth slows. I treat the '307 GW backlog' figure from one trade blog as unverified and do not use it. Scenario mean is ~$442 (0.22 x 300 + 0.53 x 435 + 0.25 x 580), and the median sits near fair value plus the dividend yield. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$436 and sigma 0.33, with 20% weight on a 1.45x-wider distribution for fat tails (capex digestion and rates), which gives P(>=432) ~0.51, down from 0.535. Research this round was limited to one filing fetch and three searches.
